scopeReview: CED FUN-7.E.1–3: initial conditions select particular solutions; definite-integral construction and domain restrictions. Standard smooth cases, positive-root branch consistency and an invalid initial point; no blanket uniqueness claim for every possible equation and no BC method.
varietyReview: Six independently differentiated initial-value candidate sets plus pole/domain analysis, lost equilibrium, shifted tangent interval, non-elementary FTC representation and undefined initial datum. Includes negative signs, nonzero initial input and branch restrictions; all four choices separately explained.
repetitionReview: Each prompt and all four options were read separately; distinct tasks/contexts within this set. Cross-topic exact duplicates checked by validator. Semantic similarity and AP difficulty remain judgment calls, not proven by an automated score.

questions.independentReasoning: Independently differentiate 3e^(x²) to obtain 6x e^(x²)=2xy. All offered functions equal 3 at zero, so checking the initial value alone would not select an answer. Separate exact differentiation and varied-input numerical checks distinguish every alternate formula.
optionReview: Its derivative has twice the required rate.
The additive shift makes the original equation fail away from x=0.
Its rate is y rather than 2xy.
The integrated exponent is x² and the initial condition fixes the multiplier at 3.

optionReview: The pole at 0 separates the positive-input branch containing x=1.

This interval excludes the initial input x=1.

optionReview: It solves the equation but has initial value +2.

optionReview: Its value at zero is 5, not 4.

It has the wrong sign at the initial point.

Separation gives 2√y=x²/2+6 and hence √y=3+x²/4.
